title: Introduce request-flame-sampler and annotated-log-collage dashboard
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Add request-level flame scoring metric and a new Grafana panel (annotated-log-collage) to stitch logs, token-phase timing and cost heatmaps for long-tail debugging. Backwards-compatible. No API surface break.
description:
Context and motivation: Production SREs and on-call engineers frequently need to understand why a small fraction of requests (the long tail) drive disproportionate token cost and latency. Existing telemetry surfaces separate token-cost histograms, spans, and log samples, which makes triage slow. This PR introduces a lightweight sampling pipeline ("request-flame-sampler") that scores invocations by a compact flame-signature and produces an "annotated-log-collage" UI that coalesces: compact token-phase timelines, top-k kernel hotspots, and joined log snippets from correlated services. Goal: speed mean time to resolution for tail incidents and provide an actionable artifact for postmortems.

Summary of changes: 1) Runtime: add request_flame_score metric and sparse flame vector in invocation envelope; sampling gate at sampler_budget_ms to limit overhead. 2) Collector: a new collector worker that aggregates flame vectors and KV-references, compresses into a compact envelope and uploads to observability store. 3) Dashboard: add an "annotated-log-collage" Grafana panel and a heatmap panel that maps flame bands to token cost buckets. 4) Alerts: introduce a scoped alert rule that fires when high flame_score percentiles correlate with token-cost SLO breach for >5m (auto-suppress for noisy routes). 5) Tests and docs: unit tests for sampler gating and an ops playbook describing costs, retention, and runbook steps.

Commits (high-level): - 1a2b3c4: introduce flame scoring function and deterministic bucketing - 2b3c4d5: add sampler API hook and config (sampler_budget_ms) - 3c4d5e6: collector worker and compression codec for flame envelopes - 4d5e6f7: grafana panel JSON and dashboard wiring - 5e6f7g8: alerts and alert-suppression policy - 6f7g8h9: tests, docs, and runbook

Files touched (high level): - runtime/src/telemetry/flame_scorer.rs (core scoring) - runtime/src/config/sampler.rs (config + gating) - collector/src/workers/flame_uploader.go (aggregation/compression) - observability/dashboards/annotated-log-collage.json (new panel) - observability/alerts/flame_alerts.yaml - tests/sampler_budget_test.go - docs/ops/annotated_log_collage_runbook.md

Performance and safety notes: The scorer uses only metrics already available in the request envelope (phase timings, token counts, model variant classifier) and a fixed-size sketch of phase deltas (<=64 bytes). Sampling is gated by a configurable budget (default 10ms per 10k requests) and can be disabled cluster-wide. Compression uses a lossless LZ-based codec with an additional small delta-encoding for KV references. Memory allocations for collector worker are bounded by stream-chunking and a soft cap; telemetry engineer sign-off required for increasing retention.

Testing and CI: Initial CI run failed on a flaky integration test (tests/integration/collector_e2e) due to a race in the test harness. Reproduced locally, added a deterministic latch, and re-ran pipeline; final CI: all checks passed. Unit tests for scorer and gating added; dashboard JSON validated with linting tool.

Review conversation (summary): - Diego Morales (reviewer): "Concern: sampling overhead and native memory pressure on high-throughput hosts. Please add a safety gate and default off for dedicated low-latency hosts." Author reply (Ava): "Added sampler_budget_ms with a default conservative budget and a runtime flag to disable on dedicated pools. Collector worker clips payload sizes and uses streaming upload to avoid spikes." Diego: "LGTM after verifying budget toggles." - Priya Desai: "Please add an e2e that verifies the pipeline under synthetic spike and an ops snippet for investigating an alert." Author: "Added collector_e2e with deterministic latch and included a runbook under docs/ops. Also added dashboard links to incident templates." - Ruth Kline: "Nit: dashboard panel labels inconsistent with existing panels." Author: "Fixed labels and added a legend consistent with 'invocation' naming conventions."

Backward compatibility and migration: No changes to public API surface. The sample envelopes are optional fields; older collectors ignore them. Dashboard and alert additions are additive. Ops note: retention defaults to 7 days for sampled envelopes; configurable in observability tier settings.

Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (canary): enable on 5% of hosted clusters for 48 hours - Stage 2: expand to 30% and run synthetic spike tests - Stage 3: enable cluster-wide with monitor thresholds - Feature gate present to fully disable for Dedicated/private installs.

Operational runbook (short): 1) When flame alert fires, open annotated-log-collage for affected route and timeframe. 2) Inspect top flame bands and kernel hotspot overlay. 3) Use provided log links to jump into correlated service logs. 4) If sampling budget spikes, reduce sampler_budget_ms or disable gate on the affected pool.

Related work and references: ENG-6543 (investigate long-tail token drivers), PM-121 (observability priority), references to prior token-attribution efforts in the repo (invocation-cost-explorer subsystems).

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main on 2026-02-16 after approvals from reviewers and green CI.
